sections.content: How many people are "gardeners and landscape gardeners"?

135,075 people

were counted on the census as "gardeners and landscape gardeners" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Gardeners and landscape gardeners cultivate flowers, trees, shrubs and other plants in public and private gardens, construct features to improve the appearance of existing terrain, and cut and lay turf.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "gardeners and landscape gardeners" there were more men than women (85.5% compared with 14.5%).

This means "gardeners and landscape gardeners" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled agricultural and related trades".

Men made up 85.5% and women made up 14.5% of "gardeners and landscape gardeners"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "gardeners and landscape gardeners" included:

  • elementary cleaning occupations (other)
  • sports players
  • process operatives (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "gardeners and landscape gardeners" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "gardeners and landscape gardeners", 15.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "gardeners and landscape gardeners" was 16 to 19 years.

  • library clerks and assistants
  • glass and ceramics makers, decorators and finishers
  • construction operatives (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "gardeners and landscape gardeners" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "gardeners and landscape gardeners" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "gardeners and landscape gardeners", 11.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (59% compared with 41%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (67.7%) than an employee (32.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
